items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: Yes Milt Hinton would be. He would definitely be.

ctx.x: Well listen you’ve been called and you are the world’s most recorded drummer. If we could assemble a rhythm section of the world’s most recorded individual people, who would be playing with you? Do you suppose Milt Hinton would be there?

Well yeah, yeah. Ooh. Wow. Yes Milt Hinton would be. He would definitely be. And then you have folks like people that they forgot about. Bob Bushnell. Bob Bushnell was the first to crack from the upright bass to the Fender. Yeah. Ooh. He did it. And he was the first to do it for ten years. He was doing it almost ten years before it really became popular. So and then you’ve got Bucky Pizzarelli on guitar, you’ve got Eric Gale, I put them all in the same category. Piano, Hank Jones. Jorge Dalto, Richard Tee. I…
Oh yeah, I forgot about him.
